title: The month of Chet
hookLine: in Chet, remember the Lord and great joy comes (Barah Maha, ang 133)

lines: THE COLD GONE, WHEAT GOING GOLD.
CHET: MARCH INTO APRIL IN PUNJAB.
LONGING IN THE SEASON OF PLENTY.
cards: The cold has finally gone. Mustard fields that were yellow all winter are going to seed. Wheat is turning gold and heavy, a few weeks from harvest.
Trees push out new leaves overnight, and the koel, a bird with a rising call, starts singing in the mornings. This is Chet, roughly March into April in Punjab, when everything seems to come back.
And Guru Arjan begins his year of longing here, in the season when you'd think nobody has any reason to long for anything.

teach.b: Chet is the first month in Guru Arjan's Barah Maha, and the Nanakshahi calendar begins its year with Chet too.

The stanza on ang 133 opens, in paraphrase: in Chet, by worshiping the Lord of the universe, a deep and lasting joy arises. Then it says how. Meeting the holy ones, the One is found, and the tongue repeats the Name.
Those who have found their Lord, their coming into the world is counted. To live even a moment without the One is to waste a life.

The One is present in water, on land, in the sky and in the forests, and those who don't keep the One in mind suffer much pain. It closes with a wish: I touch the feet of whoever brings me to meet that Lord in Chet.
Notice the joy. It isn't the joy of the season, the sunshine and new leaves.

Spring is everywhere, in water, land, sky and forest, because the One is everywhere in it, so the green outside becomes a reminder of what's inside it. Some Punjabi listeners also hear a play of sounds.
Chet is the month, but chet is also an everyday word for awareness, for keeping something in mind, as in chete, remembering.
The stanza never says it's a pun, so it's only a sound worth noticing. In the season when the world wakes up, the soul is asked to wake up too.

how: On the sangrand of Chet, gurdwaras that keep the day read the Chet stanza of Guru Arjan's Barah Maha, and in the Nanakshahi calendar Chet is the first month of the year.

the harvest month of the Vaisakhi fair

games.q: it's spring, the wheat is turning gold, and life feels full. what does the Chet stanza point you toward?
o: enjoy the season; there's nothing to long for.
remember the One in it, and find deep joy.
wait for a harder month to pray.
games.why: in Chet, by worshiping the Lord of the universe, deep joy arises. the One is in the water, land, sky and forest.

practice: Picture a seed, what you'd plant, where, how deep; a pot will do, or even a kitchen scrap like a green onion root in water.
As you picture it, breathe slowly and think of one thing in you that's been waiting to grow, and let the seed hold that wish. If you pray, you can say Waheguru over it.

wordCard.voice: Chet. Spring, the first month of Guru Arjan's Barah Maha: remembering the One brings deep joy, and the One fills water, land, sky and forest.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: in Chet, the spring month; the stanza's first word.

carryVoice: Your line: chet: joy. It comes from remembering, not from the weather. Day five hundred sixty-six: spring has started.
